title: Cuts out after a few minutes
body: Update: After some investigation I believe the problem could be related to one of two possible causes. 1. The radio does not draw enough power and the so the power bank turns off thinking there is nothing there. (Probably not the issue as I did get it to run the radio for an hour once) 2. The radio has a charge circuit so if you are using rechargeable batteries you can recharge it via the usb port. There were no batteries in the radio and I turned the charge feature off (necessary if you use alkaline batteries) but the problem still persisted. The issue is likely that the radio functionality and the power bank just do not working well together. Everything else I plugged into the powerbank worked fine. In the end it did not work for what I needed it for so I returned the device and ordered something from SAFULE. I am raising my rating to 3 stars and giving a neutral rating as I think it is just a matter of it not working for this one specific case. Original Review This power bank came with an 80% charge out of the box. Before using it I charged it to full capacity. Next I tested it on a small radio. The radio ran for 5 - 10 minutes and then shut off indicating low battery but the power bank was still showing 100% charge. I unplugged everything and reconnected  it using the second USB A output and had the same issue. The radio's USB input is 5V, 250 mA The strange thing here is that I also tried plugging in a USB fan after unplugging the radio  and that worked without issue. I have an older, less powerful power bank so I gave that a try to see if the problem was with the cable or radio. This time the radio played without issue for 30 minutes at which point I turned it off. Tried the INIU power bank again and this time it seemed to work fine as I left the radio to play for over an hour. (The power bank screen showed 99% at this point). I am going to test it out a few more times but for now I can't recommend it as reliability seems to be an issue.

body: Warning:  After having it a while, I have edited this review to include the observation that this WILL NOT CHARGE a low load device!  My hearing aid earbuds go into a charging case that connects to USB; the case charges them fast, but obviously these are very small batteries!  This battery bank thinks there is no load and shuts off as if it was left idling.  So it cannot charge the hearing aids! Original review The first thing I noted was that it arrived with zero charge (literally 0% displayed)...something I have never seen on a lithium battery device shipped to me, and fully discharged is not good for a lithium battery!  Perhaps it uses power while sitting on the shelf?  In which case, expect to find it dead whenever you take it out after storing for a while? Second thing noted was how VERY slowly it charges.  Actually fairly painfully slow...plugged into a normal USB-A, it gained 20% in 2 hours.  Connecting to a high speed charger improved it, but be forewarned. And the third thing was that using it to charge my phone from 80% to 100% dropped the charger to 70%.  My phone is 4400mAH, so it should have taken only 900mAh to charge...meaning the charger should have dropped well under 10%, not 30%.  So I question its' true capacity. I will update this as I explore this, but wanted to get this out ASAP.

productTitle: INIU Portable Charger, 22.5W 10000mAh Small USB C Power Bank Fast Charging PD3.0 QC4.0, 3-Output Battery Pack Charger Portable with Phone Holder
title: Quality and features are not as expected and marketed
body: I recently purchased a power bank and have been rigorously testing it with various devices and under different conditions. Unfortunately, the experience has been quite disappointing due to several significant issues. Here’s a detailed review highlighting the problems I encountered: ### 1. Poor Quality Cable and Alignment Issues The power bank comes with a USB A to USB C cable. Right from the start, the cable felt subpar in quality. When attempting to insert the cable, it doesn’t align smoothly, creating noticeable resistance. Thinking the problem might be with the cable itself, I tried two other cables. However, the issue persisted, indicating that the construction of the power bank's ports is flawed, causing these alignment and resistance problems. ### 2. Underwhelming Output from USB A Port The power bank advertises a 22.5W output from the USB A port. However, upon monitoring the performance, it became evident that the actual output is significantly lower. This discrepancy affects the charging speed and efficiency, falling short of the promised specifications. ### 3. Insufficient Capacity for Multiple Devices One of the key selling points of this power bank was its ability to charge two 5000mAh devices. In practice, it barely manages to charge a single 5100mAh device before depleting its power reserves. This indicates a substantial overestimation of its capacity, resulting in suboptimal usage. With a fully charged power bank, I expected to at least charge one device completely and still have some power left for another, but that hasn’t been the case. ### 4. Prolonged Charging Time Charging the power bank itself is a painfully slow process. Using a 15W charger, which is the maximum it supports, it still takes several hours to fully charge. This long charging time is highly inconvenient, especially when in need of a quick power top-up. ### 5. Overheating Display Another concerning issue is the overheating of the display while the power bank is charging. The display gets alarmingly hot, making it unsafe to carry in a pocket during charging. This overheating not only poses a potential safety risk but also reflects poorly on the device’s overall build quality. ### Conclusion Given these significant issues—poor cable quality and port alignment, lower than advertised output, insufficient capacity, prolonged charging time, and overheating display—I cannot recommend this power bank. It fails to deliver on its promises and performs below expectations in critical areas. For a reliable and efficient power bank, I suggest looking for a product from a more reputable brand that prioritizes quality and performance.
reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on 18 May 2024

productTitle: INIU Portable Charger, 22.5W 10000mAh Small USB C Power Bank Fast Charging PD3.0 QC4.0, 3-Output Battery Pack Charger Portable with Phone Holder
title: Broken after a week (stuck in a permanent charging cycle)
body: The media could not be loaded. I was excited this power bank has usb-pd support (fast charging) and is on the smaller and less heavy side. Sadly my excitement was completely ruined when I tried charging it and its code got fully hard stuck in a charging cycle. Over a month later it still says it has 78% with a blinking 8 as if it's plugged into a USB port and charging. It no longer charges (at least it doesn't report any change) and it will not charge any device I plug it into, on the USB-c port or the usb-a type outputs. Since its code is stuck in this charging routine, it also cannot be turned off. Multiple single presses of the power button, a very long press (minutes long) and a single press do nothing to get it out of its state. Unfortunately, since it also is powered by a fairly large battery bank and the display takes almost no power, I have had it on my desk for a month and it has not ran out of power (and even if it did it would possibly permanently damage the battery) I can only attribute all of this to cheap or poor coding practices on the device that led to it breaking in this extremely short period in time. Although its specs look good, I would not recommend users buy this item until they resolve this issue (and any other outstanding ones of which I'm sure exist) Oh also there's guides online that say to connect a cable between the usb-c port and A-type and this does nothing in my case (just for those who might think of that solution). Update, it took a month or two for it to fully run out of battery but when I charged it back up after it worked again which confirms my original hypothesis. If any others run into this issue know it may fix itself when it runs out of battery, though it will take quite a while and possibly damage the battery in the process

productTitle: INIU Portable Charger, 22.5W 10000mAh Small USB C Power Bank Fast Charging PD3.0 QC4.0, 3-Output Battery Pack Charger Portable with Phone Holder
title: Buyer Beware
body: The product charges my iPhone 11 Pro beautifully, and I would give it 5 stars if rating for that alone, in spite of their false claim that it charges in 30min. It does charge quickly, but not quite that fast. The 2 banks I purchased arrived with about a 54% charge on them and that was enough to charge my iPhone from 30% power twice. The issue is with recharging the power bank itself. It comes with a cord, but nowhere in the description does it tell you that if you don’t use a USB plug with a rating of 2A or higher (turns out mine are all 1A), the bank will stop charging in the 80% range. I was told this after contacting the company when I noticed BOTH banks I purchased quit charging. The company states also that the banks should be fully dead before recharging in their explanation of why they might not be fully recharging for me. If you unplug it and plug it back in, it will finish charging, but don’t think you can plug it in when you go to bed and have it recharged when you wake up.  The company’s answer to the recharging problem is that I need to go buy 2 usb blocks (My wife and I are about to go traveling abroad and both need one) rated 2A or higher. I will probably return these. I need something I can rely on to fully charge while I sleep without me having to wake up an hour early to unplug and plug back in for that last 15-20% of power.

productTitle: SURITCH Clear Case Compatible with Beats Fit Pro Cover [Slim-Fit] [Anti-Fall] [Not Easy to Dirty],Shockproof TPU Protective Portable Case with Clip Keychain for Beats Fit Pro(Stone Purple)
title: I'm not impressed
body: I'm afraid this product was not for me. I must admit I probably didn't fully pay attention to what I was ordering; I liked the idea of being able to clip my headphone case to a belt loop. In the box, you get two pieces of the case, which attach to your Beats Fit Pro headphone case using small 3M tape patches, along with a carabiner. The black parts of the case are made of a slightly more rubbery material than the Beats case, while the clear parts are simply clear plastic. So, I don't like the case for the following reasons: I've been happily slipping my headphones into my trouser pockets. Adding the extra case makes them feel surprisingly bulkier and less comfortable to slide into a pocket, especially with the carabiner attached. While 3M makes very good products, I don't trust the small tape patches in this case to keep my expensive headphones safe. I won't trust this case clipped to my belt loop, as I believe there's a risk of ending up with just the case itself, and my headphones fallen out and lost for good. Considering that the Beats case has performed well, it seems unnecessary and wasteful to encase it within another case, especially at the relatively high price of £14.99. If you're looking for a case for your Beats Fit Pro headphone case, this product might be suitable for you. However, I won't be using it moving forward, and I'm concerned that many of these will end up in landfill due to the reasons mentioned. Therefore, I cannot recommend this product.
reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on 26 September 2023

productTitle: SURITCH Clear Case Compatible with Beats Fit Pro Cover [Slim-Fit] [Anti-Fall] [Not Easy to Dirty],Shockproof TPU Protective Portable Case with Clip Keychain for Beats Fit Pro(Stone Purple)
title: So Many Issues…Where Do I Begin?
body: Appearance wise, the case is not a case at all; it’s two separate pieces of plastic that are to be secured (with poor adhesion) by 3M strips; one to cover the top of the authentic original Beats Fit Pro case, and one to adhere to the bottom of the case. It looks awkward at best. The “fit” doesn’t fit. It doesn’t cover the entire case. It is poorly designed. When installed correctly, with precision, it is nearly impossible to open without potentially damaging the original magnetic charging case. After following all installation instructions to the letter, my brand new Beats Fit Pro wouldn’t charge consistently with this product in place. Sometimes it wouldn’t charge at all with the product installed. Nothing was obstructing the port or c cable. I cannot speak to how portable the product is; given all the issues, the only place I took the item was to the UPS Store for a return. They initially promised a swift credit to my Amazon account(within two to four hours), but now they are saying it could take up to thirty days to process. Do yourself a favor and search for a different hard case, keep the original charging case in a pocketed zip organizer with your cables/peripherals when it’s not in use, or just use caution. Life is too short to waste time and money on a product that causes more problems than it solves. Stay safe, consumers. *Note: I will update this review if/when I actually receive my refund (Amazon credit).
reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on 1 July 2024
